name: TX-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: Colin Allred's large fundraising advantage ($7.4M raised)
Open seat after Crockett's retirement, but seat stays with the incumbent party
model.rationale: This Dallas-area seat carries an 18-point Democratic lean, and the fundamentals-only margin of roughly 29 points suggests the open-seat transition does little to change the underlying partisanship. Allred's name recognition and heavy fundraising against an underfunded Republican reinforce a Safe D rating, consistent with markets pricing near 97%.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or an unexpectedly strong national GOP environment could narrow the margin, though a flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jasmine Crockett (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jasmine Crockett's retirement leaves this Dallas-based district open, but the seat remains firmly Democratic territory with an 18-point partisan lean. Former Rep. Colin Allred, the Democratic nominee, enters with strong name recognition and a major financial edge, having raised about $7.4 million, while Republican Patrick Gillespie has reported little fundraising activity.

No public general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and prediction markets, which price Democrats near 97%. The expected margin is roughly 24 points, keeping the race firmly in the Safe D category despite the open-seat dynamics.
